meta.task_prompt:
This repo's own README, in the "Status" section, flags a real gap: "there's no
authentication in front of the UI or API, so don't expose the collector
Service outside the cluster without putting your own auth in front of it."

Fix that. Add authentication in front of the collector's HTTP surface:

- The JSON/query API under `internal/collector/queryapi` and
  `internal/collector/ingest`.
- The server-rendered HTMX/Alpine UI under `internal/collector/ui`.

Use a simple, self-hosted scheme appropriate for a homelab project — a
token or basic-auth credential supplied via config/env, checked in
middleware — not an external OAuth provider. Wire it through the same
config mechanism the rest of the collector's settings already use (check how
existing ConfigMap-driven settings are read). Make sure the agent-to-collector
ingest path (`POST /api/v1/logs`) still works — that's service-to-service, not
a browser, so it likely needs its own credential rather than sharing the UI's.

This repo has real test coverage and a real convention for it. Match that
convention:

- Add table-driven `_test.go` files for the new middleware/auth logic, in the
  same style as the existing tests in `internal/collector/*`.
- Run `go test ./...`, `make vet`, and `make fmt` before finishing, and make
  sure all three are clean — don't declare the task done otherwise.
- Update `deploy/k8s/*.yaml` and the README/config docs if the new auth
  setting needs to be provided at deploy time.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly
what you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and
body verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal
note.

code_review.summary: The Go side is solid and does what task.md asks. There are two stdlib middlewares in internal/collector/auth.go: Basic Auth for the UI and query API, and a separate Bearer token for POST /api/v1/logs. Credentials are compared in constant time. Wrapping happens at each call site, so the `instrument` metric labels don't change, and /healthz, /readyz and /metrics stay open. Config is loaded with the same flat-struct getEnv/getEnvInt style (plus a new getEnvBool). collector.New fails fast on half-configured auth. The agent sends the shared token through forwarder.Options, and the collector_test.go route-protection tables are a useful end-to-end check. The problem is in the Kubernetes wiring. The collector Deployment (envFrom secretRef) and the agent DaemonSet (secretKeyRef) both require the new tracer-collector-auth Secret, and neither is marked optional. The feature is sold as opt-in and off by default, and the DaemonSet comment calls the token a 'harmless no-op' when auth is disabled. But if that Secret doesn't exist, the collector pod and every agent pod fail to start, and the Secret template itself tells operators not to apply it as-is. That is a one-line fix per manifest, and I'd block on it. The rest are low: the new middleware unit tests are separate functions rather than the table-driven form task.md asked for, some tests claim more than they check, and one table field is dead.

findings.summary: The collector Deployment and agent DaemonSet both hard-require the new tracer-collector-auth Secret (no `optional: true`), so if the Secret is missing, both workloads fail to start even with AUTH_ENABLED=false.
findings.failure_scenario: A homelab operator doesn't want auth yet, so they leave AUTH_ENABLED="false". collector-secret.yaml opens with 'MUST be replaced before applying ... Do not ... apply this file as-is', and the README says to generate the Secret out of band. So they skip applying that file, or they upgrade by re-applying only the changed Deployment/DaemonSet manifests. The kubelet then marks the collector pod (envFrom secretRef, collector-deployment.yaml:39-40) and every tracer-agent pod (secretKeyRef, agent-daemonset.yaml:46-50) as CreateContainerConfigError: secret "tracer-collector-auth" not found. Log collection stops cluster-wide. This contradicts the DaemonSet comment 'Harmless no-op when the collector has auth disabled' and the PR's claim that the feature is opt-in and backward compatible.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `optional: true` under the `secretRef` in collector-deployment.yaml and under the `secretKeyRef` for AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN in agent-daemonset.yaml. With auth off, a missing Secret then just means empty env vars. collector.New's fail-fast check still catches AUTH_ENABLED=true with no credentials.

findings.summary: task.md explicitly asks for table-driven tests for the new middleware, but auth_test.go has 11 near-identical standalone functions (build cfg, build request, assert status).
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime impact. It misses the stated test-shape requirement, and adding a case means copying a 13-line function. collector_test.go in the same PR already uses table-driven t.Run subtests, so the file isn't consistent with its own sibling. It does match the older per-function style in ingest/queryapi tests, which is why this is low.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse into two tables, TestBasicAuthMiddleware and TestTokenAuthMiddleware, with fields {name, enabled, user, pass or header, wantStatus, wantWWWAuth}, and run them with t.Run.

findings.summary: The three 'DifferentLength' tests claim to verify constant-time comparison, but they only assert a 401 for wrong credentials, which the existing wrong-credential tests already cover.
findings.failure_scenario: The comment 'Ensures timing-constant comparison is used' is misleading. If secureCompare were replaced with a plain `==`, these tests would still pass, so they give false assurance about a security property.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop them, or fold them into the table as ordinary wrong-credential rows and remove the constant-time claim from the comment. If the property matters, test secureCompare directly with a small table of (a, b, want).

findings.summary: The `expectNoWWWAuth` table field is `true` in every row, so it's a dead parameter rather than a varying input.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime impact. Readers may think some rows expect a WWW-Authenticate header on the ingest path when none do.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the field and assert unconditionally that the token-auth 401 has no WWW-Authenticate header.

findings.summary: TestForwarderSendsAuthTokenInHeader and TestForwarderSendsNoAuthHeaderWhenTokenEmpty are about 30 identical lines each and differ only in the token and the expected header.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime impact. It's duplicated polling and server setup that would drift if the forwarder test harness changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into one table-driven test with rows {token: "secret-token", want: "Bearer secret-token"} and {token: "", want: ""}.

process_review.summary: The run had a sensible structure. The orchestrator ran an `ask` survey, then gave the coder a detailed, fact-filled spec. After that, the tester and reviewer ran automatically. The coder was efficient: it read each target file once before editing (0 read-before-edit violations), made about 20 targeted edits, and ran `go test ./...` (trace line 146), `make vet` (150) and `make fmt` (152), all ok:true with clean output. The tester re-ran all three after adding its own tests (281, ok:true). It also caught that `make fmt` is only `gofmt -l .` and exits 0 even when a file is listed (line 253 listed collector_test.go). It fixed that with `gofmt -w` (255) and re-verified (260, 281). So the task's 'all three clean' requirement really was met on the final tree. Most of the waste is in the ask agent. It used `search` with pattern '.' as a file lister, including a roughly 264k-character dump of internal/collector (line 5). It repeated that on deploy/k8s (lines 3, 40), searched README.md three times before reading it, and made a few failing calls. The tester also re-ran the full suite more often than needed. Judges raised nothing actionable. Two judge calls failed with empty responses (lines 115, 222) and the run carried on correctly. The reviewer approved without shell access and missed the non-optional Secret references. At about $1.55, 153 tool calls and about 12.6 minutes wall time for a 15-file, +580-line change, the budget was proportionate.

findings.summary: The ask agent ran `search` with pattern '.' over all of internal/collector as a file lister, which dumped every line of every file (about 264k chars) instead of calling list_files.
findings.evidence: Line 5: search {"pattern": ".", "path": "internal/collector"}. The paired judge record at line 4 shows "truncated": true, "original_chars": 263957. It then ran a second search {"pattern": "^package", ..., "glob": "*.go"} at line 8 to get the package list it actually wanted.

findings.summary: The ask agent repeated its earlier match-everything search of deploy/k8s, then made two more searches just to enumerate manifest files.
findings.evidence: Line 3: search {"pattern": ".", "path": "deploy/k8s"} (judge line 2: original_chars 21395). Line 40: search {"pattern": ".", "path": "deploy/k8s", "glob": "*.yaml"} (judge line 39: original_chars 21393), then line 42 ('^\\S.*\\.yaml$|^deploy/k8s', no matches) and line 44 ('kind:'). One list_files call would have answered this.

findings.summary: README.md was searched three times with overlapping regexes before the agent just read the 28-line section it needed, and the loop_control judge scored it as repeating itself.
findings.evidence: Lines 41, 43 (no matches), and 46 all search README.md for HTTP_ADDR|RETENTION_DAYS|Configuration variants. read_file README.md offset 92 at line 50 finally answered the question. The loop_control judge at line 47 returned repeating_itself 0.59, the highest in the run.

findings.summary: Three tool calls failed on avoidable argument errors: list_symbols on a directory, search in a directory that doesn't exist, and remember on a directory path.
findings.evidence: Line 19: list_symbols {"path": "internal/collector/ui"} -> 'error: not a file'. Line 48: search in "docs" -> 'error: rg failed' (no docs/ directory). Line 59: remember {"path": "deploy/k8s"} -> 'error: missing file: deploy/k8s'. All three recovered without stalling the run.

findings.summary: The coder re-read files the ask survey had already covered and that it never edited, although its brief said 'FACTS ... already verified — do not re-derive'.
findings.evidence: Line 94: read_file internal/collector/ingest/http.go (result_screen judge line 93 cache_hit: true, meaning the ask agent had already read it at line 16). The coder made no edit to that file, and its own summary says 'The ingest handler ... needed zero changes'. deploy/k8s/agent-configmap.yaml (line 92) was also read and not edited. Re-reads of files it did edit are justified by read-before-edit.

findings.summary: The tester ran the full suite five times and spent extra calls counting test names after everything was already green, plus one unexplained `cd /tmp && pwd`.
findings.evidence: go test ./... at lines 202, 250, 263, 281 (the combined test+vet+fmt run, the one that mattered) and again at 294 ('go test ./... -v | tail -50'). Lines 287 and 291 grep and wc -l the '=== RUN' lines. Line 193 runs 'cd /tmp && pwd', which has no bearing on the task.

findings.summary: Two judge calls failed with empty responses (loop_control for the coder, and result_screen for a tester run at line 222). No judge produced an adverse verdict, and the run correctly carried on.
findings.evidence: Line 115: {"kind": "judge", "tag": "loop_control", "failed": true, "response": {}}. Line 222: {"tag": "result_screen", "failed": true, "response": {}} on 'go test -v ./internal/collector -run TestNew'. All other loop_control verdicts had repeating_itself at or below 0.59 and no needs_user_input spike. The merge_gate verdicts (lines 65, 162, 228, 300) didn't block.

findings.summary: The reviewer approved while saying it couldn't verify tests. It described auth_test.go as following the table-driven convention, which it doesn't, and it didn't catch that the new Secret references are non-optional despite the 'harmless no-op' comment it quoted.
findings.evidence: The reviewer read collector-secret.yaml (line 180) and the git diff (line 164). In its report it says 'agent-daemonset pulls AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN from the same Secret key, with a comment that it's a harmless no-op when auth disabled' and 'tests follow existing table-driven convention', with verdict 'approve'. It also says 'Could not independently execute go test ./..., make vet, make fmt (review tools have no shell access)'. Its merge_gate judge (line 228) scored accomplished_its_brief 0.73.

strengths: The auth design fits a homelab project: Basic Auth for browsers, a separate Bearer token for the agent ingest path, constant-time comparison, and probes and metrics left unauthenticated.
It follows the repo's existing flat-struct/env config convention and the existing `route`/`instrument` wiring without changing metric labels.
collector.New fails fast on AUTH_ENABLED=true with missing credentials, and a table-driven test covers each missing field.
The route-protection tests in collector_test.go exercise the real mux end to end, and the forwarder header behaviour is tested.

go test ./..., make vet and make fmt are verifiably clean on the final tree (trace lines 146/150/152, re-verified at 281). The tester noticed that `make fmt` exits 0 even when it lists files, and fixed the file it listed.
concerns: The Deployment and DaemonSet hard-require the tracer-collector-auth Secret. Operators who keep auth off and follow the template's 'don't apply as-is' warning get pods stuck in CreateContainerConfigError, which contradicts the opt-in and backward-compatible claim.
The middleware unit tests aren't table-driven as task.md asked, and a few tests claim to verify constant-time behaviour they can't observe.
The reviewer stage added little independent assurance: it had no shell access and missed the manifest issue.
overall_assessment.narrative: This is a clean, well-scoped auth change. The code is correct, well tested at the HTTP layer, and verified against the task's three required checks. The one thing to fix before merge is the non-optional Secret references in the Kubernetes manifests. As written, operators who want auth off can still end up with non-starting collector and agent pods, and adding `optional: true` fixes it. The run itself was reasonably economical. The coder and tester were disciplined and the tester caught a real formatting miss. Most of the waste was the ask agent using match-everything searches as a file lister, and the reviewer approving without catching the deploy-time regression.
